Procedure: Total ankle replacement, CPT 27702
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-20
Appeal Deadline: 2027-02-16

To the Aetna Appeals Review Team:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for total ankle replacement (CPT 27702), as communicated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-20. The notice states only that "the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity," without identifying which specific criterion was unmet. I am therefore addressing the criteria set out in Aetna's own published Clinical Policy Bulletin governing this procedure, and I request that if any different or additional criteria were actually applied to my case, Aetna identify them specifically in writing as part of this appeal.

Governing Policy
The medical-necessity criteria Aetna publishes for this CPT code appear in Clinical Policy Bulletin "Total Ankle Arthroplasty," Number: 0645, available at https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/600_699/0645.html. This policy explicitly lists CPT 27702 ("Arthroplasty, ankle; with implant (total ankle)") as "covered if selection criteria are met." I was unable to confirm a visible "last revised" or "effective" date on the live page itself; I ask Aetna to confirm in its appeal response the exact version and effective date of the policy applied to my request.

Below, I address each medical-necessity element quoted directly from CPB 0645, and map it to the clinical documentation already submitted with my prior authorization request.

1. "TAA is used to replace an arthritic or severely degenerated ankle"
Weight-bearing ankle radiographs obtained 2026-06-08 show "tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts," which are hallmark findings of severe, end-stage ankle arthritis/degeneration. This satisfies the requirement.

2. "Member is skeletally mature"
[Documentation confirming skeletal maturity/date of birth is not included in the clinical summary provided to me; I ask that this be confirmed from Dr. Lindqvist's chart notes already on file with the prior authorization request.]

3. "Member has with moderate or severe pain with loss of ankle mobility and function"
I have had 18 months of progressive ankle pain unrelieved by rest, ambulate with an antalgic gait limited to two blocks, and have positive provocative testing with range of motion limited by pain on examination. This documents moderate-to-severe pain with loss of mobility and function.

4. "Imaging is consistent with severe arthritis / degeneration of the ankle due to osteoarthritis (degenerative arthritis), post-traumatic arthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, or inflammatory arthritis"
The 2026-06-08 weight-bearing radiographs showing tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts document severe degenerative joint disease consistent with this criterion. [The specific etiology classification (e.g., primary osteoarthritis vs. post-traumatic arthritis) is not stated in the clinical summary provided to me; I ask that Dr. Lindqvist's operative/clinical notes, which are already part of the prior authorization file, be reviewed to confirm this classification.]

5. "Member has have failed at least 6 months of conservative management (including physical therapy by a licensed physical therapist, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, and orthoses as indicated)"
I completed 10 weeks (20 visits) of supervised, in-person physical therapy focused on ankle strengthening and balance, from 2026-05-11 to 2026-07-20, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note. I have also been on NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-08 that provided only 3 weeks of partial relief. Combined with an 18-month total symptom duration, this satisfies the policy's overall requirement of "at least 6 months of conservative management." The policy further specifies (Footnote 1) that in-person physical therapy "must be recent (within the past year), for at least 6 weeks (12 weeks with age less than 50 years or BMI greater than 40)." My BMI is 29, and 10 weeks of in-person physical therapy exceeds even the 12-week threshold that would apply if I were under 50 years of age, so this element is met regardless of my exact age. [If Aetna's determination rests on the specific 6-week vs. 12-week threshold, please confirm my date of birth on file, as this is not included in the clinical summary provided to me.]

6. "If member is diabetic, their hemoglobin A1C (HbA1c) should be less than 8 percent within 3 months prior to surgery"
[The clinical summary provided to me does not indicate a diagnosis of diabetes. If I am not diabetic, this criterion does not apply. If Aetna's file indicates otherwise, please identify the relevant HbA1c requirement so it can be addressed with current lab values.]

7. Contraindications
The policy lists specific contraindications to TAA. My records address several directly:
- "Active or prior deep infection in the ankle joint or adjacent bones" — the clinical summary confirms "no active infection."
- "Corticosteroid injection into the joint within 12 weeks of the planned arthroplasty" — my injection was administered on 2026-05-08. [Please confirm the planned/proposed surgical date on file so this interval can be calculated; if surgery is scheduled on or after approximately 2026-07-31, this contraindication does not apply.]
- I am a non-smoker with BMI 29 and no untreated substance use, as documented in the clinical summary.
- [Documentation specifically ruling out avascular necrosis of the talus, Charcot joint, vascular insufficiency, neuromuscular disease, peripheral neuropathy, prior ankle arthrodesis, psychiatric barriers to postoperative cooperation, and severe hindfoot/forefoot/knee malalignment is not included in the clinical summary provided to me. I ask that Dr. Lindqvist's full clinical and imaging records, already submitted with the prior authorization request, be reviewed to confirm the absence of these contraindications, and that any specific contraindication Aetna believes is present be identified so it can be addressed.]

Conclusion and Request
Based on the criteria published in Aetna's own Clinical Policy Bulletin 0645, the documented 18-month symptom history, imaging showing tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts, 10 weeks of supervised in-person physical therapy, 6 months of NSAID therapy, a trial corticosteroid injection, antalgic gait limited to two blocks, and absence of active infection collectively support medical necessity for total ankle replacement. I respectfully request that Aetna:

1. Reverse the denial and approve CPT 27702 as medically necessary; or
2. If Aetna maintains that specific criteria remain unmet, identify precisely which criterion or criteria from CPB 0645 (or any other policy actually applied) are not satisfied, so that my surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, and I can supply the corresponding documentation.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and advise of the applicable appeal review timeframe. This appeal is submitted within the stated deadline of 2027-02-16.

Sincerely,

Cameron Carter
Member ID: W665314167

Enclosures: Physical therapy discharge note (2026-05-11 to 2026-07-20); weight-bearing ankle radiograph report (2026-06-08); medication/injection records; clinic notes from Dr. Lindqvist, MD [to be enclosed/confirmed]
